validated_results.title: Coffee, tea, caffeine intake, and the risk of cancer in the PLCO cohort.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting risk of incident prostate cancer by caffeine intake in the PLCO cohort.

cases.excerpt: In the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian cancer screening trial, of the 97 334 eligible individuals, 10 399 developed cancer. Cancers included were 145 head and neck, 99 oesophageal, 136 stomach, 1137 lung, 1703 breast, 257 endometrial, 162 ovarian, 3037 prostate, 318 kidney, 398 bladder, 103 gliomas, and 106 thyroid.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Similarly, a decreased kidney cancer risk due to tea intake was also suggested in a pooled analysis of 13 prospective studies (RR=0.85, 95% CI=0.71, 1.02; Lee et al , 2007 ).

design.excerpt: We investigated the relation between coffee and tea consumption and cancer in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial (PLCO) prospective study.

timing.excerpt: We investigated the relation between coffee and tea consumption and cancer in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial (PLCO) prospective study.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The diet history questionnaire administered beginning in 1998, included information on numerous food items including coffee, tea, and caffeine intake.
